# B.O.B. Community Code of Conduct

B.O.B. is intended to be useful to people with different working styles, backgrounds, abilities, and levels of technical experience. Participation in this project should make collaboration easier, not more exhausting.

## Expected behavior

Be respectful, specific, and constructive. Critique ideas and implementations rather than people. Assume good intent without requiring anyone to tolerate repeated harmful behavior. Make room for questions, different communication styles, and accessibility needs. Keep technical disagreements focused on evidence, tradeoffs, and the goals of the project.

## Unacceptable behavior

Harassment, threats, discriminatory language, sexualized attention, deliberate intimidation, doxxing, repeated personal attacks, or publishing another person's private information are not acceptable. Neither is using issue or review processes primarily to provoke, derail, or exhaust other contributors.

## Project spaces

This code applies to repository issues, pull requests, discussions, reviews, project-managed community spaces, and other spaces where someone is representing B.O.B. or participating in an official project activity.

## Enforcement

Maintainers may edit, hide, lock, or remove content; reject or close contributions; restrict participation; or take other proportionate action when behavior conflicts with this policy.

Sensitive conduct reports should not be filed as public issues. Contact the repository owner privately using the contact information available through the owner's GitHub profile. Reports will be handled as confidentially as reasonably possible.

## Intent

The goal is not ceremonial paperwork. It is a clear promise that contributors can disagree, ask basic questions, report problems, and participate without being treated like an inconvenience.
